_note: The MAINNET deployment of the channel contract, as a record a reader can re-derive.
Same purpose as `sepolia.json`: a public document can cite a file instead of restating a hex
string, and the deployment's own working files are gitignored, so without this record the tree
cannot show that the contract exists and 'absent from tracked source' reads as 'not deployed'.
Every value below was read from a node with the query beside it, not copied from a document.
Re-derive it: run the queries in `verified_by` against `rpc` and compare.
THE CLASS HASH IS NOT SEPOLIA'S. Sepolia carries 0x07d2f324…4467, the version with a `u64`
counter in storage; that counter was removed before this deployment, so mainnet carries a
different class. `scarb build && sncast utils class-hash --contract-name Channel` on the
tracked source reproduces the value below, which is the check that this record is honest.
strk20.json now lists this contract and the five mainnet message hashes; this file is the
deployment record behind them, carrying the declare/deploy detail a submission manifest has
no field for. The five are direct privacy_invoke calls, NOT routed through the STRK20 pool -
there is no mainnet pool route from this client - and the root README states that beside
them so neither file implies more than happened.

deployed_by._type_note: INVOKE because the deploy went through an account, via the universal deployer. It is the transaction that deployed the contract; calling it 'the deploy transaction' is loose.

_note: Paid, not estimated. Predicted from a local devnet rehearsal before spending: declare 0.5842,
deploy 0.0347. The declare came in 1.6% UNDER; the deploy came in 7.4% OVER. An earlier version
of this note said 'both came in under', which was wrong about the deploy in both size and sign.
`l1_gas` was 0 on every transaction, so none of this is exposed to Ethereum L1 gas.
The account itself was counterfactual - funded but never deployed - so its DEPLOY_ACCOUNT is
part of what this deployment cost and is recorded rather than netted out.
_per_message_note: MEASURED ON MAINNET, from five real publishes, not estimated. Each cost 0.031062 STRK with
l1_gas 0, l1_data_gas 128, l2_gas 1,097,280 - identical across all five.
This field previously read 0.028133 and was derived from a devnet rehearsal. It was 10.4% low:
the same class costs 11.8% more l2_gas on mainnet than on devnet. Devnet is the right instrument
for comparing two contracts against each other and the wrong one for an absolute price.

verified_by: starknet_call(<contract.address>, selector('privacy_invoke'), [0x1234, 0x5678]) -> ['0x0'] — the empty open-note deposits array a pool-routed publish requires

starknet_getEvents(address=<contract.address>, from_block=<deployed_by.block_number>, to_block=latest) -> exactly 5 PointerPublished events, keys[0] = starknet_keccak('PointerPublished'), one per hash in messages.transaction_hashes
starknet_getNonce(latest, deployer) -> 8 == 1 DEPLOY_ACCOUNT + 1 DECLARE + 1 deploy + 5 publishes; the public post added none, because a post never touches the chain

_note: Five real channel publishes, the first traffic on this contract. Neither felt in a
PointerPublished event names a sender or a recipient; that is the design, so these
transactions demonstrate the chain path and disclose no counterparty.
